source.title: The Heterogeneous Safety Impacts of Benign Multilingual Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Will Hawkins; Kai Rawal; Jonathan Rystrøm; Stratis Tsirtsis; Zi-Hao Fu; Greta Warren; Ryan Brown; Eoin Delaney; S. Wachter; Brent D. Mittelstadt; Christopher Russell

record.tranche_reason: The study measures a contrastive adversarial-minus-non-adversarial hidden-state direction and relates its drift after fine-tuning to adversarial compliance. It does not intervene on the direction, so it conceptually tests the proposed direction-behaviour relationship rather than reproducing the causal ablation/addition method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports several SORRY-Bench compliance results for multilingual fine-tuning, but those results alone do not test the direction claim. The rows below are limited to the mechanistic results relating contrastive-direction displacement to compliance. Direction-selection and layer-selection details are not additional outcome rows.
record.test_reason: The study builds an adversarial-minus-non-adversarial difference-in-means direction (Eq. 2) as an analysis tool. It measures how far that direction drifts, as a PCA distance, after benign multilingual LoRA fine-tuning, then correlates drift magnitude with change in SORRY-Bench compliance. It never ablates or adds the direction, never checks whether the direction mediates refusal, and never compares single-direction and multi-direction accounts. A correlation between drift magnitude and compliance change cannot show whether ablating the direction removes refusal or adding it induces refusal. The measure is a representational-displacement score rather than a test of mediation, so it does not test V1 or any other version.
record.authors_conclusion:
Largely right, but it understates the main conclusions. The authors' headline findings are:
- Benign multilingual fine-tuning shifts adversarial compliance heterogeneously by fine-tuning and evaluation language, up to four-fold.
- This safety drift is decoupled from capability.
- English-only fine-tuning and evaluation gives inadequate safety assurance.
- Small internal drift buffers or compromises alignment depending on architecture.
The authors make no claim about whether a single direction mediates refusal.
record.recipe_differences: The study computes adversarial-minus-non-adversarial hidden-state directions and measures their drift after benign multilingual LoRA fine-tuning; it does not use the original direction ablation or addition intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: The direction-displacement/compliance relationship differs by model architecture: it is inverse for the two larger models Gemma-3-4B-IT and Qwen3-4B, opposite for both Llama models, and not consistent for Gemma-3-1B-IT or Qwen3-0.6B.

fits_no_version.finding: After benign multilingual LoRA fine-tuning, the relation between drift of the 80th-percentile-layer harmful-minus-harmless direction and English compliance change depends on architecture. In Gemma-3-4B-IT and Qwen3-4B, small drift goes with more refusal. In both Llama-3.2 models, small drift goes with more compliance. Gemma-3-1B-IT and Qwen3-0.6B show no consistent relation. English fine-tuning gives the largest drift yet stays closest to baseline compliance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Magnitude of drift in the difference-in-means refusal direction under benign fine-tuning predicts change in refusal rate, with a sign that depends on the model.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The direction-compliance findings are correlational and do not test causal mediation. The mechanistic analysis uses 44 adversarial and 44 non-adversarial prompts; exact Figure 4 values and uncertainty for the reported model-specific trends are not stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No other directional mechanistic outcomes were reported in a form bearing on V1. General compliance changes following benign fine-tuning, capability evaluations, vector-selection cosine results (Appendix A.5), and PCA variance/clustering descriptions (Appendix A.6) do not test whether the direction causally mediates refusal.

untested.parts: Ablation removing refusal, addition inducing refusal, and preservation of other abilities are all untested; only drift of the direction under fine-tuning is measured.
Multilingual setting, but the study does not test whether a refusal direction carries across languages; it measures only English-prompt directions.
Benign fine-tuning shifts compliance, but the study does not test whether training determines the existence of a single removable direction.

record.verdict_notes: The study cites Arditi et al. and uses its difference-in-means construction, computed on only 44+44 prompts. Drift is summarised as Euclidean distance in a 2D PCA space pooled across fine-tuned models. This is a magnitude measure, so it cannot show whether the direction mediates refusal. The SORRY-Bench compliance results are behavioural and do not bear on the direction claim. The reader's 'tests/T2' and V1 links are not supported.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures direction drift and its relationship to compliance, but does not ablate or add the direction, establish causal mediation, or test whether other abilities remain intact.
Jailbreak suppression of the direction and robustness training against its ablation are not tested.
The study does not compare affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts of refusal.
The study does not separate harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
The study does not test transfer of a refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
Benign multilingual fine-tuning is tested, but the study does not test how or when refusal training determines whether a single removable direction exists.

rows.subject: Gemma-3-1B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Measured displacement of an adversarial-minus-non-adversarial hidden-state direction after fine-tuning and related it to change in English adversarial compliance.
rows.measure: Relationship between contrastive-direction displacement and change in adversarial compliance
rows.baseline: Base model compliance; exact value not stated here
rows.value: No consistent relationship between displacement magnitude and compliance is observed, despite large safety deviations.
rows.note: The prose explicitly describes the lack of a consistent relationship. This is correlational and does not establish whether the direction mediates refusal.
rows.check: Measure is drift magnitude vs. compliance change, with no intervention on the direction; it cannot show V1's ablation or addition effect. Baseline is base-model compliance, not a no-ablation control.

rows.subject: Qwen3-0.6B
rows.operation_detail: Measured displacement of an adversarial-minus-non-adversarial hidden-state direction after fine-tuning and related it to change in English adversarial compliance.
rows.measure: Relationship between contrastive-direction displacement and change in adversarial compliance
rows.baseline: Base model compliance; exact value not stated here
rows.value: No consistent relationship between displacement magnitude and compliance is observed, despite large safety deviations.
rows.note: The paper also notes signs of general degradation for this model, including reduced non-adversarial compliance.
rows.check: Same as r1. The authors also attribute Qwen3-0.6B's compliance drop to general model collapse, not to anything about the direction.

rows.subject: Gemma-3-4B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Measured displacement of an adversarial-minus-non-adversarial hidden-state direction after fine-tuning and related it to change in English adversarial compliance.
rows.measure: Relationship between contrastive-direction displacement and change in adversarial compliance
rows.baseline: Base model compliance; exact value not stated here
rows.value: Larger displacement correlates with a return toward baseline compliance; smaller displacement is associated with increased refusals.
rows.note: The stated relationship is correlational; no direction intervention establishes mediation.
rows.check: Correlational drift-magnitude result; no ablation or addition. Figure 4 values are not stated in the text.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Measured displacement of an adversarial-minus-non-adversarial hidden-state direction after fine-tuning and related it to change in English adversarial compliance.
rows.measure: Relationship between contrastive-direction displacement and change in adversarial compliance
rows.baseline: Base model compliance; exact value not stated here
rows.value: Minimal displacement corresponds to the largest increases in adversarial compliance, while larger displacements restore refusal behaviour.
rows.note: This is the opposite trend to that described for Gemma-3-4B-IT and Qwen3-4B, but remains correlational.
rows.check: Correlational drift-magnitude result; no ablation or addition. Figure 4 values are not stated in the text.
